statement: The managed split of a user table under write load (ManagedSplitWorkflow, src/partition/managed-split-workflow*.js) resumes rather than re-plans and never cuts over onto an unroutable child: the persisted split plan (SPLIT_KEY, TARGET_PARTITION_IDS) is resolved before the workflow registers and rides every transition row a retry writes — pending, admission-blocked, deferred, preparing — so a retry after a routable-wait timeout (run 2026-08-30T12-07-55: deferred at W+6:20, admission-blocked retry, re-plan at W+6:36 leaving four overlapping v2 rows) resumes the same children (typed PERSISTED_PLAN_RESUMED) and no key is ever covered by two v(N+1) rows; and SPLIT_CUTOVER_ACTIVE is written only when every child's canonical leader service is serve-routable per the query plane's routing snapshot, re-evaluated inside the owner lane with the existing 30-second provisioning budget and 50 ms poll (run 12-23-20: cutover applied and source dissolved while the right child's leader was readiness-denied), otherwise the workflow stays pre-cutover with the source serving and the CATCHUP_READY ack carrying a typed cutoverReadiness refusal (SPLIT_CUTOVER_READINESS_DECISION / SPLIT_CUTOVER_REFUSAL_REASON). The healthy split path's event sequence, budgets, cadences, dispatch ordering, readiness rules and the 60-second certification window are unchanged; ManagedSplitWorkflow remains the sole split lifecycle authority. Proven deterministically on the real workflow: red on HEAD (re-plan observed; cutover applied under denial), green after.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

A split retry never plans new children while the durable transition row carries SPLIT_KEY/TARGET_PARTITION_IDS; every row a retry writes (pending, blocked, deferred, preparing) carries the persisted plan; at most one pair of v(N+1) rows exists per split source and no key is covered by two v(N+1) rows.

SPLIT_CUTOVER_ACTIVE is written only when every child's canonical leader service is serve-routable per the query plane's routing snapshot, re-evaluated inside the owner lane; otherwise the workflow stays pre-cutover, the source keeps serving, and the ack carries a typed cutoverReadiness refusal.

The readiness wait reuses the existing provisioning budget (30 s) and poll cadence (50 ms); no new budget, timer, cadence, readiness rule or dispatch ordering is introduced; the 60-second GCP certification window is unchanged; the healthy split path's event sequence is byte-identical to HEAD.

ManagedSplitWorkflow remains the sole split lifecycle authority; PartitionService, readiness, and routing contribute evidence only; nothing derives cluster-ACTIVE or READY from nodes.status, publication counts, or coverage.

Proof is a deterministic witness on the real ManagedSplitWorkflow reproducing runs 2026-08-30T12-07-55 and 12-23-20 (routing-timeout deferral + admission-blocked retry; cutover with a readiness-denied child leader), red on HEAD (3/6) and green after (6/6), with the healthy-sequence and budgets controls that must stay green; no GCP run is part of the proof.
